day1.name: Back Width
day1.sessionWhy: The back is the foundation of the V-taper. Wide lats make the waist look tiny. This session builds width, corrects forward posture, and creates the silhouette that makes everything else look better.
day1.phaseNote: Feel every rep. Build the mind-muscle connection with your lats before loading heavy. The stretch at the bottom of every pull is where the growth happens.

ex1.name: Weighted Pull-Up
ex1.why: Number 1 lat width exercise. Dead hang at bottom fully stretches the lat. Stretched position is where hypertrophy signalling is highest. Cannot be replicated on a machine.

sub1.name: Lat Pulldown
sub1.exp: Same movement pattern on a machine — great if pull-ups are too difficult.

sub2.name: Assisted Pull-Up
sub2.exp: Use the assisted machine to build toward full pull-ups.

sub3.name: Cable Pullover
sub3.exp: Isolates the lat in the stretched position.

ex2.name: Cable Straight-Arm Pulldown
ex2.why: Isolates the lat without bicep involvement. Teaches your brain to feel the lat working which is critical for mind-muscle connection in Phase I.

sub1.name: DB Pullover
sub1.exp: Lie on bench, arc the dumbbell behind your head to stretch the lat.

sub2.name: Band Pulldown
sub2.exp: Same movement with a resistance band.

sub3.name: Straight-Arm Cable Pushdown
sub3.exp: Cable version from a high pulley.

ex3.name: Chest-Supported T-Bar Row
ex3.why: Chest support removes the lower back from the equation so the mid-back does all the work. Builds the 3D thickness that makes your back look like a wall from behind.

sub1.name: Seated Cable Row
sub1.exp: Sit at a cable station, pull to your lower chest with elbows flared 45 degrees.

sub2.name: Chest-Supported DB Row
sub2.exp: Lie chest-down on an incline bench holding dumbbells.

sub3.name: Machine Row
sub3.exp: Any chest-supported row machine.

ex4.name: Face Pulls
ex4.why: Directly counters forward shoulder posture. Strengthens rear delts and mid traps which are the two muscles most responsible for standing tall and looking confident.

sub1.name: Band Pull-Apart
sub1.exp: Pull a resistance band apart at chest height keeping arms straight.

sub2.name: Reverse Fly Machine
sub2.exp: Sit facing the machine and fly the pads apart.

sub3.name: Cable Reverse Fly
sub3.exp: Cables crossed, pull apart with straight arms.

ex5.name: Single-Arm Cable Row
ex5.why: Unilateral work fixes left-right imbalances. One side is always stronger from daily life and this equalises both sides for symmetrical width.

sub1.name: Single-Arm DB Row
sub1.exp: One knee and hand on bench, row the dumbbell to your hip.

sub2.name: Single-Arm Band Row
sub2.exp: Anchor a band and row with one arm.

sub3.name: Single-Arm Machine Row
sub3.exp: Use one arm at a time on any row machine.

ex6.name: Cable Rear Delt Row (Wide Grip)
ex6.why: Second rear delt movement of the session. You can never do too much rear delt work. Protects the shoulder joint long term and continues building posture.

sub1.name: Reverse Pec Deck
sub1.exp: Sit facing the pec deck machine and reverse the motion.

sub2.name: DB Rear Delt Fly
sub2.exp: Hinge forward 45 degrees and fly dumbbells out to the sides.

sub3.name: Band Reverse Fly
sub3.exp: Same motion with a resistance band.

day2.name: Legs — Quads
day2.sessionWhy: Quads are your biggest muscle group so they need the most volume and the most food. Today is quad-dominant. Two dedicated leg days per week is the scientifically proven fastest way to build powerful legs.
day2.phaseNote: Full depth on every squat. Full range of motion builds significantly more muscle than partial reps at heavier weight. Leave your ego at the door this phase.

ex1.name: Barbell Back Squat
ex1.why: The king of all exercises. Releases more testosterone and growth hormone than any other movement. High bar and upright torso keeps the load on the quads rather than the lower back.

sub1.name: Goblet Squat
sub1.exp: Hold a dumbbell at your chest and squat — great for beginners to learn the pattern.

sub2.name: Smith Machine Squat
sub2.exp: The fixed bar helps you focus on depth and form.

sub3.name: Leg Press
sub3.exp: Sit in the leg press and push the platform away — feet low and narrow for quad focus.

ex2.name: Leg Press (Feet Low & Narrow)
ex2.why: Feet low and narrow on the platform shifts all the stress onto the quads. Perfect substitute for hack squat and allows heavier loading than split squats for raw mass.

sub1.name: Hack Squat Machine
sub1.exp: If available this is the best option — same foot position.

sub2.name: V-Squat Machine
sub2.exp: Similar to hack squat, great for quad isolation.

sub3.name: Smith Machine Squat (Feet Forward)
sub3.exp: Place feet slightly in front and let the bar track to load quads.

ex3.name: Bulgarian Split Squat
ex3.why: Research confirms unilateral training builds more muscle per leg than bilateral squatting alone. Also fixes the imbalances most people develop from daily movement patterns.

sub1.name: Reverse Lunge
sub1.exp: Step back into a lunge keeping torso upright for quad focus.

sub2.name: Step-Up with Weight
sub2.exp: Step onto a bench holding dumbbells.

sub3.name: Single-Leg Leg Press
sub3.exp: One leg at a time on the leg press.

ex4.name: Leg Extension (Slow Eccentric)
ex4.why: 3-second lowering maximises time under tension at the stretched position. Builds the quad sweep visible from the front and the separation between the quad heads.

sub1.name: Sissy Squat
sub1.exp: Lean back and let your knees travel far forward — intense quad isolation.

sub2.name: Cyclist Squat
sub2.exp: Heels elevated on plates, narrow stance squat — quad dominant.

sub3.name: Wall Sit with Weight
sub3.exp: Hold a plate on your thighs for added resistance.

ex5.name: Standing Calf Raise
ex5.why: Full stretch at the bottom is the only way to actually grow calves. Most people do partial reps which only maintains them. Hang your heel off the edge for maximum stretch.

sub1.name: Seated Calf Raise
sub1.exp: Targets the soleus underneath — do both standing and seated for complete calves.

sub2.name: Leg Press Calf Raise
sub2.exp: Push the platform away with just your toes.

sub3.name: Smith Machine Calf Raise
sub3.exp: Stand on a plate under the smith bar.

ex6.name: Ab Wheel Rollout
ex6.why: Trains your core to resist extension which is the exact demand when carrying heavy loads. Builds the deep ab strength that protects the lower back and also creates core density.

sub1.name: Cable Crunch
sub1.exp: Kneel at a high cable and crunch your ribs to your hips.

sub2.name: Plank with Weight
sub2.exp: Standard plank with a plate on your back.

sub3.name: Dead Bug
sub3.exp: Lie on your back and alternate extending opposite arm and leg.

day3.name: Chest & Arms
day3.sessionWhy: Upper chest gives the illusion of a bigger fuller physique even with a shirt on. Arms are trained here so they get direct work without overlapping with back day. Zero heavy oblique work ever in this program — it widens the waist permanently.
day3.phaseNote: Superset the arm exercises at the end to save time and create a massive pump that accelerates growth. Focus on the stretch at the bottom of every pressing movement.

ex1.name: Incline Barbell Press
ex1.why: Upper chest is the most underdeveloped area in most lifters. A full upper chest creates the shelf look and makes the chest visible when standing upright. 30–45 degree incline is the scientifically proven sweet spot for upper pec activation.

sub1.name: Incline DB Press
sub1.exp: Dumbbells allow a greater range of motion and fix left-right imbalances.

sub2.name: Incline Smith Machine Press
sub2.exp: The fixed bar removes balance demands so you can focus purely on the chest.

sub3.name: Cable Upper Chest Fly
sub3.exp: Cables from low to high hitting upper chest with constant tension.

ex2.name: Incline DB Fly
ex2.why: The wide arc creates maximum stretch on the pec fibres. Stretched position training triggers satellite cell activation which is the mechanism behind actual muscle fibre growth not just swelling.

sub1.name: Cable Fly High to Low
sub1.exp: Cables set high, fly down and across — constant tension throughout.

sub2.name: Pec Deck at Incline
sub2.exp: If the machine adjusts to incline, use it for the same stretch.

sub3.name: Resistance Band Fly
sub3.exp: Anchor bands behind you and fly your arms together.

ex3.name: Cable Crossover (High to Low)
ex3.why: Cable provides constant tension throughout the entire movement which dumbbells cannot. Builds the lower chest separation line visible when you take your shirt off.

sub1.name: DB Fly Flat
sub1.exp: Lie flat and fly dumbbells in a wide arc.

sub2.name: Pec Deck Machine
sub2.exp: Sit and squeeze the pads together — great constant tension.

sub3.name: Push-Up with Weight
sub3.exp: Elevate feet and place weight on back for added resistance.

ex4.name: Close-Grip Bench Press
ex4.why: Triceps make up two thirds of your upper arm. Close grip bench allows the heaviest loading of any tricep exercise — more weight equals more mechanical tension equals more growth.

sub1.name: Weighted Dips
sub1.exp: Lean slightly forward and dip with weight between legs or on a belt.

sub2.name: DB Tricep Press (Close Grip)
sub2.exp: Dumbbells touching together on a flat bench.

sub3.name: Smith Machine Close Grip
sub3.exp: Fixed bar helps keep elbows tucked.

ex5.name: Overhead Cable Tricep Extension
ex5.why: The only movement that fully stretches the tricep long head. The long head is the biggest of the three heads and gives the horseshoe shape when developed. Must be trained in the stretched position.

sub1.name: Overhead DB Tricep Extension
sub1.exp: Hold one dumbbell with both hands behind your head.

sub2.name: EZ-Bar Overhead Extension
sub2.exp: Same movement with a barbell — more stable.

sub3.name: Band Overhead Extension
sub3.exp: Anchor a band at your feet and extend overhead.

ex6.name: Incline DB Curl
ex6.why: Arm positioned behind the body on the incline bench creates a full stretch on the long head of the bicep. The long head is what creates the peak when you flex. Flat curls completely miss this stretch.

sub1.name: Cable Curl from Low Pulley
sub1.exp: Stand at a cable machine and curl — constant tension throughout.

sub2.name: Spider Curl
sub2.exp: Lie chest-down on an incline bench and curl — removes all cheating.

sub3.name: Band Curl Seated
sub3.exp: Sit on a bench with band under your feet.

ex7.name: Hammer Curl
ex7.why: Neutral grip trains the brachialis which is the muscle underneath the bicep. When the brachialis develops it physically pushes the bicep upward making your arms look significantly thicker from every angle.

sub1.name: Rope Hammer Curl
sub1.exp: Use the rope attachment on a low cable.

sub2.name: Cross-Body Hammer Curl
sub2.exp: Curl across your body to emphasise the brachialis.

sub3.name: Reverse Curl
sub3.exp: Overhand grip on a barbell or cables to hit brachialis and forearms.

day4.name: Legs — Hamstrings
day4.sessionWhy: Posterior chain day. Weak glutes cause anterior pelvic tilt which makes the stomach stick out even when lean. Build this posterior chain and you stand taller and look leaner automatically without changing anything else.
day4.phaseNote: The RDL is the most important exercise of the day. Spend extra time feeling the hamstring stretch at the bottom. That stretched position is exactly where the muscle grows.

ex1.name: Romanian Deadlift
ex1.why: The best hamstring exercise in existence. The deep stretch at the bottom fully loads the hamstrings in their lengthened position. Science confirms stretched-position training builds significantly more muscle than contracted-position training.

sub1.name: Dumbbell RDL
sub1.exp: Same movement with dumbbells — great if you are learning the hinge pattern.

sub2.name: Single-Leg RDL
sub2.exp: One leg at a time for maximum hamstring stretch and balance challenge.

sub3.name: Cable Pull-Through
sub3.exp: Stand facing away from a low cable and hinge forward.

ex2.name: Leg Curl Unilateral (Lying)
ex2.why: Forces each leg to work independently. Most people have a significantly weaker hamstring on one side from daily movement patterns. This identifies and fixes the imbalance before it becomes an injury.

sub1.name: Nordic Curl
sub1.exp: Kneel on a pad with feet anchored and lower your body forward — brutally effective.

sub2.name: Swiss Ball Leg Curl
sub2.exp: Lie on your back with heels on a ball and curl it toward you.

sub3.name: Resistance Band Leg Curl
sub3.exp: Anchor band at ankle height and curl.

ex3.name: Barbell Hip Thrust
ex3.why: EMG research confirms hip thrusts produce higher glute activation than any other exercise including squats. Strong glutes mean upright posture, no lower back pain, and powerful athletic movement.

sub1.name: DB Hip Thrust
sub1.exp: Same movement with dumbbells on your hips.

sub2.name: Single-Leg Hip Thrust
sub2.exp: One leg at a time — doubles the intensity and fixes imbalances.

sub3.name: Cable Pull-Through
sub3.exp: Face away from cable and hinge to squeeze glutes at the top.

ex4.name: Good Morning
ex4.why: Builds the spinal erectors which are the muscles running alongside your spine. Directly translates to better posture and protects the lower back during any heavy physical activity.

sub1.name: Back Extension
sub1.exp: Lie face down on a hyperextension bench and extend your body up.

sub2.name: Cable Pull-Through
sub2.exp: Same hip hinge pattern with a cable for constant tension.

sub3.name: Dumbbell Good Morning
sub3.exp: Hold dumbbells at shoulders instead of a barbell.

ex5.name: Seated Calf Raise
ex5.why: The bent knee position deactivates the gastrocnemius and isolates the soleus which sits underneath. You need both heads of the calf trained for complete calf development visible from every angle.

sub1.name: Leg Press Calf Raise (Seated)
sub1.exp: Sit in the leg press with knees bent and press with toes only.

sub2.name: Resistance Band Seated Calf Raise
sub2.exp: Sit on a bench with band looped over your knees and press down.

ex6.name: Hanging Leg Raise
ex6.why: Posterior pelvic tilt at the top is what makes this effective — without it you are just swinging your hip flexors. Lower abs are the last part of the six pack to appear and the hardest to develop.

sub1.name: Captain Chair Leg Raise
sub1.exp: Same movement on a captain chair machine.

sub2.name: Reverse Crunch with Weight
sub2.exp: Lie on a bench and crunch your hips up toward the ceiling.

sub3.name: Cable Crunch from Low Pulley
sub3.exp: Pull the cable toward your hips while lying down.

day5.name: Shoulders & Back Thickness
day5.sessionWhy: Wide shoulders complete the V-taper. Combined with back thickness today your upper body will look wide and powerful from every angle. This is the session that makes the physique look complete.
day5.phaseNote: Lateral raises are the single most important exercise for shoulder width. Never go heavy enough that you swing. Slow and controlled with a slight lean away is what actually builds the side delt.

ex1.name: Seated DB Overhead Press
ex1.why: Seated position removes the ability to use leg drive so it is pure shoulder work. Dumbbells allow a natural arc that protects the rotator cuff compared to a fixed barbell path.

sub1.name: Barbell Overhead Press
sub1.exp: Standing or seated with a barbell — allows heavier loading.

sub2.name: Smith Machine OHP
sub2.exp: Fixed bar path helps beginners learn the pressing motion.

sub3.name: Cable Overhead Press
sub3.exp: Cables from the sides pressing up — constant tension.

ex2.name: Cable Lateral Raise (Unilateral)
ex2.why: Cable provides constant tension throughout the entire movement while dumbbells have zero tension at the bottom. The side delt is the muscle that creates visible shoulder width and this is the single most important exercise for looking broader.

sub1.name: DB Lateral Raise
sub1.exp: The classic — slight lean away and slight bend in elbow.

sub2.name: Machine Lateral Raise
sub2.exp: Great for beginners — removes the stability challenge.

sub3.name: Band Lateral Raise
sub3.exp: Anchor band under your foot and raise to the side.

ex3.name: Seated Cable Row (Wide Grip)
ex3.why: Wide grip and elbows flared 45 degrees hits the mid-traps and rhomboids specifically — the muscles that hold your shoulders back and create back thickness from behind.

sub1.name: Barbell Row Overhand
sub1.exp: Hinge forward and pull bar to lower chest.

sub2.name: T-Bar Row
sub2.exp: Chest on the pad and pull the bar to your sternum.

sub3.name: DB Row
sub3.exp: One knee on bench, pull dumbbell to your hip.

ex4.name: Single-Arm DB Row (High Elbow)
ex4.why: High elbow pulling toward the hip rather than straight up hits the upper lat and teres major — the muscles that create the width right under your armpit. Most rows miss this area completely.

sub1.name: Meadows Row
sub1.exp: Load one end of a barbell and row it with high elbow — same angle.

sub2.name: High Cable Row Single Arm
sub2.exp: Set cable at shoulder height and pull across your body.

sub3.name: Machine Row Single Arm
sub3.exp: Use one arm at a time on any row machine.

ex5.name: Rear Delt Cable Fly
ex5.why: This is the third rear delt movement across the week and you need this volume to undo forward posture that builds up over months and years of daily life. Rear delts recover fast and respond to high frequency.

sub1.name: Reverse Pec Deck
sub1.exp: Sit facing the machine and reverse the pec deck motion.

sub2.name: DB Rear Delt Fly
sub2.exp: Hinge forward 45 degrees and fly dumbbells straight out to the sides.

sub3.name: Band Reverse Fly
sub3.exp: Same hinge position with a resistance band.

ex6.name: DB Shrug
ex6.why: Well developed upper traps make the physique look powerful and athletic from the front and back. Hold the peak contraction for one full second — the contracted position is where the growth stimulus is highest.

sub1.name: Barbell Shrug
sub1.exp: Allows heavier loading than dumbbells.

sub2.name: Cable Shrug
sub2.exp: Constant tension throughout the movement.

sub3.name: Smith Machine Shrug
sub3.exp: Fixed bar helps you focus on the contraction rather than balance.

ex7.name: Weighted Plank
ex7.why: Trains the transverse abdominis which is your natural weight belt. When this muscle is strong it physically cinches the waist inward. Combined with daily vacuum breathing it is the primary driver of the tiny waist goal.

sub1.name: Ab Wheel
sub1.exp: Roll out slowly and back in — trains the same anti-extension pattern.

sub2.name: Dead Bug
sub2.exp: Lie on back and alternate extending opposite arm and leg while keeping lower back flat.

sub3.name: Hollow Body Hold
sub3.exp: Press lower back into the floor and hold legs and arms extended.

day6.name: Arms & Core
day6.sessionWhy: Extra arm volume every two weeks gives biceps and triceps a dedicated session on top of the work they already get in chest day. Arms respond fastest to frequency. Core work here focuses on building actual muscle density and the TVA vacuum protocol.
day6.phaseNote: Keep this under 60 minutes. This is a bonus session — quality and feel over weight and ego.

ex1.name: EZ-Bar Preacher Curl
ex1.why: The preacher bench locks the upper arm in place completely removing any momentum or cheating. This forces the bicep to do 100% of the work through the full range of motion.

sub1.name: Machine Preacher Curl
sub1.exp: Same locked position on a machine — great for beginners.

sub2.name: Cable Preacher Curl
sub2.exp: Use a low cable at a preacher bench for constant tension.

sub3.name: DB Preacher Curl
sub3.exp: Same locked position with a dumbbell for unilateral work.

ex2.name: Cable Curl (Supinated)
ex2.why: Supinating the wrist fully at the top of the movement maximises the peak contraction of the bicep. Holding that squeeze for one second at the top creates the maximum growth stimulus at the contracted position.

sub1.name: DB Curl
sub1.exp: Standard dumbbell curl with full supination at the top.

sub2.name: Barbell Curl
sub2.exp: Allows heavier loading — great for overall bicep mass.

sub3.name: Band Curl
sub3.exp: Anchor band under foot and curl — constant tension.

ex3.name: Skull Crusher (EZ-Bar)
ex3.why: Loads the tricep long head in its fully stretched position which is where it responds best to growth stimulus. The long head makes up the majority of tricep size and gives the horseshoe shape.

sub1.name: DB Skull Crusher
sub1.exp: Same movement with dumbbells — allows arms to travel further back for more stretch.

sub2.name: Cable Overhead Extension
sub2.exp: Stand facing away from cable and extend overhead.

sub3.name: Dip
sub3.exp: Lean forward slightly to emphasise the long head.

ex4.name: Cable Pushdown (Rope)
ex4.why: Spreading the rope apart at the very bottom of each rep creates maximum lateral head contraction. The lateral head is what creates the horseshoe shape visible from the side when the arm is relaxed.

sub1.name: V-Bar Pushdown
sub1.exp: Narrow grip emphasises the lateral head.

sub2.name: DB Kickback
sub2.exp: Hinge forward and extend the arm straight back.

sub3.name: Band Pushdown
sub3.exp: Anchor band overhead and push down.

ex5.name: Cable Crunch (Kneeling)
ex5.why: Weighted ab work builds actual ab muscle density. You cannot have impressive abs without first building the muscle under the fat. Training builds the muscle and diet reveals it.

sub1.name: Decline Weighted Crunch
sub1.exp: Lie on a decline bench holding a plate on your chest.

sub2.name: Machine Crunch
sub2.exp: Sit in an ab machine and crunch — great for beginners.

sub3.name: Ab Roller
sub3.exp: Roll out and back — similar to cable crunch but bodyweight.

ex6.name: Hanging Leg Raise
ex6.why: Lower abs are the last section of the six pack to appear and the hardest to actually develop. Posterior pelvic tilt at the top is essential — without this cue you are training hip flexors only.

sub1.name: Captain Chair Raise
sub1.exp: Same movement on a captain chair machine for beginners.

sub2.name: Reverse Crunch
sub2.exp: Lie on a bench and crunch the hips up — bodyweight version.

sub3.name: Cable Crunch Low Pulley
sub3.exp: Pull the cable toward hips while lying on the floor.
